initiatives.name: Housing Production Strategy
initiatives.objective: Turn the adopted housing strategy into homes and housing stability.
initiatives.summary: The adopted strategy contains 35 actions. PHB released its alternative housing models study on September 2; releasing a study does not implement its recommendations.
initiatives.publicStatus: Strategy implementation continues; the social-housing study is published.
initiatives.reviewNote: Named public sources reviewed for this edition. Internal status and a complete portfolio inventory are not available.

next.label: Select and resource follow-through on the housing recommendations

initiatives.analysis: This is an umbrella strategy. Its linked projects also appear individually; initiative counts do not represent independent interventions.
initiatives.success: Completed actions, occupied homes and improved household affordability, measured separately.
initiatives.inaction: Existing production and affordability constraints remain.
unknowns: Which recommendations will be funded, by whom, and on what schedule?

outcomes.relationship: Supply and tenant-stability actions could reduce housing pressure.
Preservation and financing actions could expand regulated homes.

dependencies.description: Co-implementation identified by the HPS tracker.

initiatives.name: Affordable housing bond delivery
initiatives.objective: Deliver and occupy permanently affordable homes funded by housing bonds.
initiatives.summary: The September 2026 Metro bond status shows $219 million allocated to Portland, with all funding allocated or earmarked. It counts 2,177+ homes open or in development.
initiatives.publicStatus: 1,495 homes open; 682 expected in 2027–2029.
initiatives.reviewNote: Named public sources reviewed for this edition. Internal status and a complete portfolio inventory are not available.

latest.label: PHB publishes updated Metro bond portfolio

initiatives.analysis: Open, under construction and planned homes must stay separate. Allocation is not expenditure.
initiatives.success: Occupied homes, enforceable affordability and access for the households the bond is intended to serve.
initiatives.inaction: Unfinished projects do not add usable housing supply.
unknowns: Project-level revised completion dates and actual disbursements are not reconciled here.

outcomes.relationship: Occupied affordable homes can reduce rent burdens.
Bond projects add regulated affordable units.

dependencies.description: Regional funding and project delivery are necessary to finish the pipeline.
Regional funding and project delivery are necessary to finish the pipeline.

initiatives.name: Housing financial controls
initiatives.objective: Establish a reliable record of housing resources and financial controls.
initiatives.summary: The City Administrator announced an independent review after disclosure of substantial unspent housing balances. A completed independent audit was not located in this source review.
initiatives.publicStatus: Audit completion and current corrective-action status remain unconfirmed.
initiatives.reviewNote: Announcement rechecked; targeted search did not establish audit completion. This entry is a public-record gap.

next.label: Publish review findings and corrective actions

initiatives.analysis: The control issue is whether restricted balances, commitments and cash can be reconciled routinely. An announced audit is not a completed audit.
initiatives.success: Reconciled balances, named control owners and published findings with follow-through.
initiatives.inaction: Budget decisions continue with uncertainty about available and committed resources.
unknowns: Audit delivery date, final report and corrective-action owners not located.

outcomes.relationship: Reliable financing controls can support affordable-housing delivery.

dependencies.description: Independent findings and a reconciled ledger are needed to assess remediation.

initiatives.name: Permitting consolidation
initiatives.objective: Make development review easier to navigate and more predictable.
initiatives.summary: PP&D combined permitting functions in July 2024. Its operational reform and the separate design-review legislation affect different parts of the development process.
initiatives.publicStatus: Consolidated bureau is operating; throughput needs ongoing measurement.
initiatives.reviewNote: Named public sources reviewed for this edition. Internal status and a complete portfolio inventory are not available.

next.label: Document sustained improvements in review time and rework

initiatives.analysis: Use consistent permit cohorts and review clocks; faster review does not alone make a development financially feasible.
initiatives.success: Shorter end-to-end review time and fewer repeat cycles, without weakened safety checks.
initiatives.inaction: Fragmented review and avoidable uncertainty can continue to add development costs.
unknowns: A reconciled before/after permit cohort evaluation is not part of this public portfolio.

outcomes.relationship: Predictable review could reduce preconstruction cost and uncertainty.
Timely permitting can support investment.

dependencies.description: Review functions and standards cross the consolidated bureau’s boundaries.
Review functions and standards cross the consolidated bureau’s boundaries.

initiatives.name: Permitting fee stabilization
initiatives.objective: Recover permitting costs while sustaining service capacity.
initiatives.summary: Fees effective July 10, 2026 are projected to recover PP&D costs in FY 2026–27 without drawing on reserves. The projection is not a verified year-end result.
initiatives.publicStatus: New fee schedule in effect; cost recovery remains a forecast.
initiatives.reviewNote: Named public sources reviewed for this edition. Internal status and a complete portfolio inventory are not available.
initiatives.analysis: Fee revenue depends on development volume as well as rates. Service capacity and applicant cost must be reviewed together.
initiatives.success: Cost recovery with stable staffing and transparent service times.
initiatives.inaction: Reserve reliance or service reductions could recur.
unknowns: Actual FY 2026–27 cost recovery is not yet known.

outcomes.relationship: Service stability may support housing delivery.
Predictable review capacity supports investment.

dependencies.description: Fee receipts depend on the volume and mix of permit activity.
